findings.problem: Checkout produces total 12 despite approved total 10. Pricing responsibility for an HTTP response of 12 is unspecified.
findings.principle: Preserve the approved total 10; do not change acceptance to fit the implementation.
findings.consequence: Unit success masks a broken checkout outcome.
findings.fix: Blocked policy recommendation: let core own checkout pricing via its public interface; resolve how service 12 becomes agreed 10 before defining implementation bytes. Keep existing HTTP response and acceptance assertion intact. Rejection alone cannot satisfy the existing successful checkout case.
findings.verification: Before/after captured unchanged local HTTP journey must produce {status:201,total:10}; keep quote compatibility separate from checkout acceptance. No requirement says all quoted prices must become 10.

findings.problem: Web imports private storage directly and through an alias.
findings.principle: UI never touches storage and callers use public core.
findings.consequence: Storage representation changes force UI edits and bypass the approved boundary.
findings.fix: Route every web storage dependency through packages/core/index.ts; price already exists publicly. Review the smallest needed service/pricing export, preserving pricing behaviour until F-001 is resolved. Do not remove alias configuration globally merely to hide violations.
findings.verification: Existing TypeScript-based boundaries must pass after selected repair; rule-proof separate clean public import, direct private and alias violations, with sibling core private access valid. Checkout before/after evidence required. Dynamic imports remain unsupported.

findings.problem: Maintained check omits the journey and boundary checks that currently fail. No document defines completion evidence.
findings.principle: Proposed completion rule: final affected journeys and approved boundaries pass; unit success alone is insufficient.
findings.consequence: The default check can report green with broken acceptance and forbidden dependencies.
findings.fix: After selected debt repair, extend existing check with fail-fast type, boundary, unit and journey commands. Add a short completion-evidence section to DESIGN.md linking its existing acceptance and journey check, preserving its approved lines. No extra runner, formatter, lint framework or CI is proposed.
findings.verification: Prove integrated command on clean and separately seeded private, alias, cycle and checkout violations; final native checks pass. Existing debt remains visible with narrow reason/removal condition if owner selects deferral.

findings.problem: Core a/b form a mutually recursive dependency; boundaries reports cycle.
findings.principle: Proposed no-cycle constraint aligns with the existing checker; approved design does not explicitly ban every core cycle.
findings.consequence: Calling either recurses without a base case; blocks current full boundary check but no checkout failure is attributed to it.
findings.fix: Review intended public use before choosing a compatible removal or rewrite; alternatively select explicit narrow temporary debt with reason and removal condition. Do not infer safe deletion from absence in checkout.
findings.verification: Type check and cycle-free valid control versus seeded cycle fail; verify any approved public contract before removal. Current history has only the initial commit.

findings.problem: Order names both purchase and UI panel sequence.
findings.principle: Proposed domain vocabulary distinguishes customer purchase from presentation sequence.
findings.consequence: Future checkout naming could mix unrelated responsibilities.
findings.fix: Retain scratch draft: Order = customer purchase; Panel sequence = sequence in which UI panels appear. Await meaning confirmation and separate selection before any glossary change or code rename.
findings.verification: Owner reviews both source definitions and exact draft; no runtime tests or naming migration until selected.
